original_test_intent: Stress BMC cold-reset recovery for more than 24 hours while proving KVM/management returns after each reset and host power/device state remains unchanged.
original_method: On a dedicated host with independent recovery, issue one supported BMC cold reset, wait for bounded BMC/LAN/KVM recovery, verify host power and device invariants, capture diagnostic deltas and repeat only while the approved duration/rate and abort policy remain satisfied.
manual_activity: Approve the target, supported cold-reset command/channel/cipher, duration and reset cadence, BMC reconnect deadline, host power/device invariant matrix, KVM observation cadence and abort/recovery thresholds.

safety_requirements: Do not expose credentials or bypass host identity
Issue only one reset before validating full BMC recovery
Stop on BMC timeout, KVM loss, identity drift, host invariant change or unexpected diagnostic
agent_execution_scope: Validate cold-reset semantics and secure access
Capture BMC/KVM and host power/device baselines
Poll BMC/LAN services to bounded readiness
Verify host power and named device invariants
Verify final cleanup and archive evidence
engineer_actions: Define host invariant matrix and KVM criteria

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: `mc reset cold` matches the item, but fixed cipher 17 is unvalidated and a time-based loop without per-reset readiness can overlap resets. Its final `systemctl` check cannot prove device invariance and unsafe sshpass/host-key bypass is unacceptable.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Use the approved secret-backed BMC cold-reset command once, wait for complete BMC/LAN/KVM recovery, verify the named host power/device invariants and diagnostic delta, then continue only under the approved cadence.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: The Procedure's more-than-24-hour target is preserved; the 720-minute Machine Time conflicts with it and is not used to shorten the run. Reset count/rate and cipher are not inferred.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Treat every BMC cold reset as a bounded management outage with service-readiness checkpoints and an independent host invariant comparison before the next reset.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Replaces plaintext credentials, blind time-looping and final-only checks with secure access, per-reset recovery, KVM observation, host device diffing and abort evidence.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Validates BMC cold-reset recovery without intended host power transition; it does not test host reboot, chassis power cycle, physical AC removal or BMC firmware update.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: A reachable IPMI endpoint may precede KVM or sensor readiness, and management reset can temporarily obscure host faults. A generic OS-running result cannot establish the required device inventory invariant.

project_override_considerations: If firmware documents service-specific readiness phases after cold reset, use those deadlines separately. Preserve the Procedure's >24h requirement unless an approved decision resolves the conflicting 720-minute metadata.
expected_evidence: Approval, exact BMC/host identity and recovery readiness
Per-reset command result and BMC service recovery times
Host power state and named device-inventory comparison
Verified >24h elapsed duration and cycle count
No hardware PASS claim by the agent

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Procedure requires more than 24 hours, while Machine Time is 720 minutes (12 hours). The review preserves the explicit Procedure duration and records the metadata conflict without changing Master.

blocked_analysis.analysis: Cold-reset method, cadence, recovery thresholds and host/KVM oracles are identifiable package and approval inputs, so the case is REQUIRES rather than irreducibly BLOCKED.

review_improvement: Turns a blind BMC reset loop into a per-reset management-recovery and host-invariance test, while retaining the unresolved 24-hour versus 12-hour source timing conflict.
independent_technical_reasoning: A BMC cold reset should restart management firmware without cycling host power, making unchanged host power and device inventory central evidence rather than an incidental final check. IPMI availability alone may return before KVM, sensors and Redfish are ready, so service-specific recovery timing matters. Reissuing resets too quickly can keep the BMC perpetually degraded and invalidate endurance conclusions. The source explicitly says over 24 hours, which cannot be reconciled with 720 minutes by assumption.
